input.rationale: The interpretation of receipt ffa0ec9302fc43f89664310bd5b9a332 records one comparison violated because of my declaration, not the data: old_leader_still_leader means the old leader was seen leading at some point during the watch, which it satisfied by re-winning the fresh election, whereas the claim I meant to test is that the transfer removes the sitting leadership even though the destination cannot lead. This successor changes only the watch sampling and the field set needed for a predicate that matches the claim: states are sampled every 20ms instead of every 100ms and the summary adds leaderless_seen, so the interruption can be asserted directly, while the destination and control predicates stay as they were. Everything else - cluster, timings, the DemoteVoter step, the transfer call, the 15s future wait and the 8s watch - is unchanged, so the fresh execution is required by the field and predicate change rather than to obtain a different outcome. The earlier receipt and its interpretation stay as recorded.

scope.description: Transfer leadership to a demoted non-voter and, as a control, to a voter, recording the future's result, the states at the moment the result arrives, whether the cluster was ever without a leader during the watch, whether the requested destination ever led, and whether terms advanced.
assumptions: Real target constructors and APIs: BootstrapCluster, NewRaft, DemoteVoter, LeadershipTransferToServer, GetConfiguration, Stats; uniform HeartbeatTimeout 2s, LeaderLeaseTimeout 1s, CommitTimeout 200ms.

Only the leader is bootstrapped with the four-voter configuration, so it is the deterministic first leader; the demoted node becomes a non-voter through the public DemoteVoter call before the transfer.
The control target is a voter, so the same call shape is exercised with a suffrage the configuration honours.
The future is awaited up to 15s and the cluster then watched for 8s with states sampled every 20ms.
Transports stay fully connected and healthy throughout.
excluded: No partition, no snapshots and no client traffic besides the configuration change and the transfer call.
No production code or default is modified.

experiment.prefix: Four nodes are created (identity = in-memory transport address), wired fully connected and started; only the first is bootstrapped with the four-voter configuration so that it is the deterministic first leader. For the treatment the near node is demoted to non-voter through DemoteVoter and the harness waits until both far nodes report it without a vote. A setup CA_EVENT records the case, the target, whether the target has a vote, the leader's identity and its term. The harness then calls LeadershipTransferToServer(target) and waits up to 15s for the future, emitting transfer_result with the returned error, whether it was nil, the elapsed time and the states of the old leader and the target at that moment. It then watches the cluster for 8s sampling every 20ms, and emits transfer_summary with leaderless_seen, whether the old leader was ever seen leading again, whether the target ever became leader, the identity of any leader seen again, and whether any node's term advanced.
semantic_changes: Watch sampling interval changed from 100ms to 20ms.
transfer_summary now carries leaderless_seen: whether any sample in the watch window found no node in the Leader state.
Comparisons assert the interruption through leaderless_seen instead of through old_leader_still_leader; the destination and control predicates are unchanged.
experiment.requirement: LeadershipTransferToServer names a destination for leadership (api.go:1268-1282). A reported success should mean the requested destination took leadership, and starting a transfer must not remove the existing leadership when the named destination cannot legally lead.
experiment.responsibility: The leader's leadership-transfer path: which destination it honours, what it reports to the caller, and what the TimeoutNow and vote-request handling on the destination side does to the current leadership.

comparisons.description: Anomaly prediction: the transfer future reports success although the named destination holds no vote.
At the moment the caller is told the transfer succeeded, the sitting leader is no longer in the Leader state.
The reported success is not about the requested destination: the non-voter target never leads during the watch.
The cluster was without a leader at some sample of the watch, i.e. starting a transfer to a destination that cannot lead interrupts the existing leadership rather than preserving it.
Control: with a voter destination the same call's success is honoured by the destination actually leading.

experiment.revision_reason: The tear-down predicate was declared on a field that means 'the old leader was seen leading at some point in the watch', which the recovery satisfies; the successor samples the watch every 20ms and adds leaderless_seen so the interruption is asserted directly, and keeps only predicates whose fields mean what the claim says.

scope.description: Real 4-node in-memory cluster: elect a leader, optionally move one follower from voter to non-voter via the public DemoteVoter API, partition the cluster so the leader keeps only that node reachable, then call the public VerifyLeader API and record the future result together with the leader state. Treatment keeps a demoted (non-voter) node reachable; control 1 keeps the same reachable set but that node is still a voter; control 2 keeps the demoted non-voter but cuts the leader from every other node. On a successful confirmation the harness also waits for a leader on the far side, applies a write through the new leader and samples both FSMs.
assumptions: Real target constructors are used: BootstrapCluster + NewRaft, InmemTransport fully connected, InmemSnapshotStore, MockFSM; membership change and partition are driven only through public APIs (DemoteVoter) and the in-memory transport's documented Disconnect.

Partitions are established by removing transport routes (cluster.Disconnect / cluster.Partition helpers), i.e. the same mechanism the target's own tests use; the partition set is chosen by the harness, not by the measured result.
Timing: HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout (3s for the treatment attempts, 2s for the controls), CommitTimeout = 50ms, ProtocolVersion 3, so ValidateConfig holds for every node.

The treatment is attempted up to three times because whether a voter-majority election lands inside the partitioned leader's remaining lease window is timing dependent; the VerifyLeader result itself is recorded for every attempt.
excluded: Real TCP transports and cross-process partitions are not exercised; the in-memory transport is the target's own test transport.
No production code, configuration default or store behaviour is modified.

basis.prefix: The harness builds each cluster with MakeClusterCustom (Bootstrap: true, LongstopTimeout 60s) so all four nodes are bootstrapped with the same 4-voter configuration, then waits for a stable single leader and its followers. For the treatment and control 2 it calls leader.DemoteVoter(nearNode.localID, 0, 10s) and waits until the far side reports the node without a vote, so the leader's own quorum size is 2 of voters {leader, far1, far2}. It then partitions the cluster with cluster.Partition([leader, nearNode]) (treatment, control 1) or cluster.Disconnect(leader) (control 2), records the setup and partition as CA_EVENT lines, launches leader.VerifyLeader().Error() in a goroutine and polls the far side for a Leader state while waiting for the result. The result, the leader's state, elapsed time and whether another leader existed are emitted as a verify_result CA_EVENT. If the confirmation succeeded, the harness waits up to 4s for a far-side leader, applies 'assurance-stale-write' through it, and emits stale_read_window with both FSMs' contents, the leader's state and the applied index.
basis.requirement: A success from VerifyLeader is a confirmation that the caller may keep treating this node as leader and read its FSM (api.go:880-882 documents that purpose). Since non-voters are, by the target's own definition, 'not considered for elections or commitment purposes' (configuration.go:16-18), the confirmation must rest on acknowledgements from a quorum of voters; a non-voter's acknowledgement may not substitute for one.
basis.responsibility: Leader-side quorum confirmation consumed by the client through the public VerifyLeader API; the leader owns both the quorum arithmetic (quorumSize, voter-filtered) and the vote attribution (verifyFuture.vote, unfiltered) that decide the answer.

comparisons.description: Anomaly prediction for the treatment: the leader that can reach only the demoted non-voter answers VerifyLeader with success (nil error) while its quorum size of 2 is defined over voters {leader, far1, far2}. Satisfying this comparison supports the defect explanation; it does not by itself establish it.

Control 1 (only the suffrage of the reachable node differs): with that node still a voter the leader must not report success, because its acknowledgement belongs to the quorum that is otherwise unreachable.
Control 2 (only reachability differs): with the same non-voter suffrage but no reachable peer at all, no acknowledgement can arrive, so success must not be reported.

No change to the harness file, the cluster construction, the partition, the VerifyLeader call, the emitted event fields or the recorded sources.

scope.description: Follow one committed voter-to-non-voter transition in a healthy 4-node cluster while sampling every node's own configuration view and log index, three independent runs.
assumptions: Real target constructors and APIs only: BootstrapCluster, NewRaft, DemoteVoter, GetConfiguration, LastIndex; per-node Config values (leader 20s, near 6s, far voters 3s), all ValidateConfig-clean.

Only the leader is bootstrapped; the other three start with empty configurations and adopt them through normal replication, so the cluster is the same construction as the extended-window experiment that produced the unexplained sighting.
Before the transition the harness waits until every follower reports itself with a vote and has LastIndex >= 2, so the baseline is uniform and the transition is the only event under observation.
Sampling is every 20ms for ten seconds after the transition is committed on the leader; a node counts as converged at the first sample where its own view shows the demoted peer without a vote.
Three runs in one execution; the transports stay fully connected and healthy throughout, so any lag observed is not caused by a partition.
excluded: No partition, no snapshots, no restarts or crash-recovery, and no client traffic besides the configuration change itself.
The configuration index used for the consistency check is read from the leader after the change returns; the harness does not inspect the follower's log store directly.

basis.prefix: Four nodes are created (identity = in-memory transport address), wired fully connected and started; only the first is bootstrapped with the four-voter configuration, so it is the deterministic first leader and the others adopt the configuration through replication. The harness waits for that leader, then waits until every follower reports itself with a vote and has LastIndex >= 2, and emits a baseline CA_EVENT with each node's view of the near node and its LastIndex. It then calls DemoteVoter(near, prevIndex 0, timeout 10s), waits for the future (which returns when the entry is committed on the leader), records the leader's LastIndex as the configuration index, and polls every node every 20ms for ten seconds: each poll reads that node's GetConfiguration view of the near node's suffrage and its LastIndex. A node counts as converged at the first poll where its view shows the near node without a vote; the harness also keeps the highest LastIndex seen while that node's view was still old. One demotion_view CA_EVENT is emitted per node with converged, converged_ms, stale_observed, stale_max_last_index, the configuration index, index_passed_while_stale, and the node's end state and LastIndex.
basis.responsibility: Configuration propagation from the leader's committed membership change to each peer's own view of its suffrage, as consumed by that peer's election eligibility (runFollower checks hasVote on its latest configuration before campaigning) and by quorum arithmetic on the leader.

comparisons.description: Run 1: every node (including the demoted one) reports the new suffrage within the ten second observation window on a healthy transport; a node that never converges is contradicted here.
Run 1 consistency: no node's view may still be old at a sample where that node's own LastIndex already reached the configuration entry, which would separate a processing gap from a delivery lag.
Run 2 convergence prediction, identical predicate.
Run 2 consistency prediction, identical predicate.
Run 3 convergence prediction, identical predicate.
Run 3 consistency prediction, identical predicate.

semantic_changes: The single per-run baseline CA_EVENT is replaced by one node_baseline event per node and run, carrying case, role, node_id, the node's own view of the demoted peer (near_present, near_voter) and its LastIndex.
Prerequisites now reference node_baseline with per-run conditions; comparisons, identity fields (case, role) and applicability conditions are otherwise unchanged.
No change to cluster construction, per-node timing, the DemoteVoter call, the 20ms sampling loop, the 10s observation window or the measured fields.

basis.prefix: The harness builds each cluster with MakeClusterCustom (Bootstrap: true, LongstopTimeout 60s) so all four nodes are bootstrapped with the same 4-voter configuration, then waits for a stable single leader and its followers. scope.description: Extend the observation window of the non-voter VerifyLeader defect: cut a long-lease leader off from the voter majority while one non-voter stays reachable, ask VerifyLeader immediately, then ask again once the majority has elected a competing leader and committed a write.
assumptions: Real target constructors and APIs: BootstrapCluster, NewRaft, DemoteVoter, VerifyLeader, Apply, GetConfiguration; per-node Config values only, no production code or default changed.

Only the leader is bootstrapped with the four-server configuration (all voters), so it is the only node that can campaign initially; the other nodes start with empty configurations and adopt the configuration through normal AppendEntries replication.

The near node's voter-to-non-voter transition is the public DemoteVoter call; the harness waits until the far side reports it without a vote and records the leader's own view of that suffrage separately from the near node's self view.
Partition is imposed by removing in-memory transport routes in both directions between {leader, near} and the two far voters; the far voters keep their mutual routes.
The 20s leader lease is within ValidateConfig (LeaderLeaseTimeout <= HeartbeatTimeout) and only makes the pre-existing window observable; the defect claim does not rest on the value chosen.
excluded: No TCP or cross-host partition; no disk-backed log/snapshot store.

basis.prefix: Four nodes are created first (identity is the in-memory transport address), then wired fully connected and started; only the first node is bootstrapped with the configuration {leader, near, far1, far2} all Voter, so it wins the initial election and replicates the configuration to the others (they start empty and cannot campaign). scope.description: Follow one committed voter-to-non-voter transition in a healthy 4-node cluster while sampling every node's own configuration view and log index, three independent runs.
assumptions: Real target constructors and APIs only: BootstrapCluster, NewRaft, DemoteVoter, GetConfiguration, LastIndex; per-node Config values (leader 20s, near 6s, far voters 3s), all ValidateConfig-clean.

Only the leader is bootstrapped; the other three start with empty configurations and adopt them through normal replication, so the cluster is the same construction as the extended-window experiment that produced the unexplained sighting.
Before the transition the harness waits until every follower reports itself with a vote and has LastIndex >= 2, so the baseline is uniform and the transition is the only event under observation.
Sampling is every 20ms for ten seconds after the transition is committed on the leader; a node counts as converged at the first sample where its own view shows the demoted peer without a vote.
Three runs in one execution; the transports stay fully connected and healthy throughout, so any lag observed is not caused by a partition.
excluded: No partition, no snapshots, no restarts or crash-recovery, and no client traffic besides the configuration change itself.
The configuration index used for the consistency check is read from the leader after the change returns; the harness does not inspect the follower's log store directly.

basis.prefix: Four nodes are created (identity = in-memory transport address), wired fully connected and started; only the first is bootstrapped with the four-voter configuration, so it is the deterministic first leader and the others adopt the configuration through replication. The harness waits for that leader, then waits until every follower reports itself with a vote and has LastIndex >= 2, and emits a baseline CA_EVENT with each node's view of the near node and its LastIndex. It then calls DemoteVoter(near, prevIndex 0, timeout 10s), waits for the future (which returns when the entry is committed on the leader), records the leader's LastIndex as the configuration index, and polls every node every 20ms for ten seconds: each poll reads that node's GetConfiguration view of the near node's suffrage and its LastIndex. A node counts as converged at the first poll where its view shows the near node without a vote; the harness also keeps the highest LastIndex seen while that node's view was still old. One demotion_view CA_EVENT is emitted per node with converged, converged_ms, stale_observed, stale_max_last_index, the configuration index, index_passed_while_stale, and the node's end state and LastIndex.
basis.responsibility: Configuration propagation from the leader's committed membership change to each peer's own view of its suffrage, as consumed by that peer's election eligibility (runFollower checks hasVote on its latest configuration before campaigning) and by quorum arithmetic on the leader.

Transports stay fully connected and healthy, so any lag is not caused by a partition.
The configuration index used for the consistency check is the leader's LastIndex after the change returns.
excluded: No partition, snapshots, restarts or client traffic besides the configuration change.
No production code, default or store behaviour is modified.

prefix.before: Four nodes are created (identity = in-memory transport address), wired fully connected and started; only the first is bootstrapped with the four-voter configuration, so it is the deterministic first leader and the others adopt the configuration through replication. The harness waits for that leader, then waits until every follower reports itself with a vote and has LastIndex >= 2, and emits one node_baseline CA_EVENT per node carrying case, role, the node's own view of the near node and its LastIndex. It then calls DemoteVoter(near, prevIndex 0, timeout 10s), waits for the future (which returns when the entry is committed on the leader), records the leader's LastIndex as the configuration index, and polls every node every 20ms for ten seconds: each poll reads that node's GetConfiguration view of the near node's suffrage and its LastIndex. A node counts as converged at the first poll where its view shows the near node without a vote; the harness also keeps the highest LastIndex seen while that node's view was still old. One demotion_view CA_EVENT is emitted per node with converged, converged_ms, stale_observed, stale_max_last_index, the configuration index, index_passed_while_stale, and the node's end state and LastIndex.
prefix.after: Four nodes are created (identity = in-memory transport address), wired fully connected and started; only the first is bootstrapped with the four-voter configuration so that it is the deterministic first leader. Runs 1 and 2 wait until every follower reports itself with a vote and has LastIndex >= 2 before the transition; run_3_immediate issues the transition as soon as the bootstrapped node reports Leader, so the followers may still have empty configurations. One node_baseline CA_EVENT is emitted per node (case, role, the node's own view of the near node, LastIndex, waited_baseline), then DemoteVoter(near, prevIndex 0, 10s) is called and its future waited on, the leader's LastIndex is recorded as the configuration index, and every node is polled every 20ms for ten seconds for its own GetConfiguration view of the near node's suffrage and its LastIndex. Per node the harness emits demotion_view with converged, converged_ms, stale_observed, stale_max_last_index, config_index, index_passed_while_stale, last_index_end and state_end.

responsibility.after: Configuration propagation from the leader's committed membership change to each peer's own view of its suffrage, and the leader's replication path that must deliver that entry to every peer in the configuration.

scope.description: Transfer leadership to a demoted non-voter and, as a control, to a voter in the same kind of 4-node cluster, recording the future's result, the states of the old leader and the target, whether the target ever leads, and whether the terms advanced.
assumptions: Real target constructors and APIs: BootstrapCluster, NewRaft, DemoteVoter, LeadershipTransferToServer, GetConfiguration, Stats; uniform HeartbeatTimeout 2s, LeaderLeaseTimeout 1s, CommitTimeout 200ms.

Only the leader is bootstrapped with the four-voter configuration, so it is the deterministic first leader; the demoted node becomes a non-voter through the public DemoteVoter call before the transfer.
The target for the control is a voter, so the same call shape is exercised with a suffrage the configuration honours.

The harness waits up to 15s for the transfer future and then watches the cluster for 8s, sampling states and terms every 100ms, so a recovered cluster is recorded rather than only the immediate instant.
Transports stay fully connected and healthy throughout.
excluded: No partition, no snapshots and no client traffic besides the configuration change and the transfer call.
No production code or default is modified.

basis.prefix: Four nodes are created (identity = in-memory transport address), wired fully connected and started; only the first is bootstrapped with the four-voter configuration so that it is the deterministic first leader. For the treatment the near node is demoted to non-voter through DemoteVoter and the harness waits until both far nodes report it without a vote. A setup CA_EVENT records the case, the target, whether the target has a vote, the leader's identity and its term. The harness then calls LeadershipTransferToServer(target) and waits up to 15s for the future, emitting transfer_result with the returned error, whether it was nil, the elapsed time and the states of the old leader and the target. It then watches the cluster for 8s, sampling every 100ms, and emits transfer_summary with whether the old leader ever remained leader, whether the target ever became leader, whether any leader existed again and which node it was, and whether any node's term advanced.
basis.requirement: LeadershipTransferToServer names a destination for leadership (api.go:1268-1283). A reported success should mean the requested destination took leadership, and starting a transfer must not remove the existing leader when the requested destination cannot legally lead.
basis.responsibility: The leader's leadership-transfer path: which destination it honours, what it reports to the caller, and what the TimeoutNow and vote-request handling on the destination side does to the current leadership.

comparisons.description: Anomaly prediction for the non-voter target: the transfer future reports success even though the destination holds no vote.
The reported success is not about the requested destination: the non-voter target never leads during the watch window.

Control: the same call with a voter destination succeeds.
Control: with a voter destination the reported success is honoured by the destination actually leading.

Comparisons assert the interruption through leaderless_seen instead of through old_leader_still_leader; the destination and control predicates are unchanged.
